# nemau_instance_group (Resource)

An instance group: between `min_size` and `max_size` identical instances, created from one launch template, that scale with target-tracking policies and scheduled actions. The group is free; its instances are billed as instances are. Growing a group needs a billable organization.

**The autoscaler owns `desired_capacity`.** It is Optional and Computed: leave it out and Terraform never fights the autoscaler. Set it and Terraform sets the capacity once, at the next apply that changes it. A scheduled action or a policy then moves it again.

**Replacement.** Changing `name`, `network_id` or `subnet_id` replaces the group. Deleting a group that has members is refused unless `delete_instances_on_destroy` is true, which deletes them.

**user_data is never read back.** The platform seals the document and returns only whether one is set, and a digest of it. An import leaves the document empty: set it again after an import. The provider compares the platform's SHA-256 digest of the document with the configured one, so a document changed outside Terraform shows as a change. A group cannot lose its user_data: the plan refuses the removal, and replacing the group is the way to remove it.

A change of the launch template is a new template version. The members move to it when a rolling refresh runs: the platform starts one for a template change when `refresh_on_template_change` is true, with the group's stored `max_unavailable_pct` and `max_surge`. Without it, the new version is stored and the members keep their version until a refresh runs. The apply waits for the refresh to be accepted, not for every member to roll; the platform reports the refresh's state in the group's view.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nemau_instance_group" "web" {
  name       = "web-pool"
  network_id = nemau_network.backend.id
  subnet_id  = nemau_subnet.app.id
  min_size   = 2
  max_size   = 6

  # Omit desired_capacity: the autoscaler decides it. Set it to move it once.
  security_groups = [nemau_security_group.web.id]

  launch_template {
    image_id  = data.nemau_images.debian.images[0].id
    flavor_id = "small"
    key_name  = "deploy"
    # cloud-init document of each member; never returned by the API.
    user_data = file("${path.module}/cloud-init.yaml")
  }

  load_balancer_pool {
    pool_id       = nemau_pool.web.id
    protocol_port = 80
  }

  scaling_policy {
    metric         = "cpu_percent"
    target         = 60
    window_seconds = 300
  }

  scheduled_action {
    cron     = "0 8 * * 1-5"
    min_size = 4
  }

  scheduled_action {
    cron     = "0 20 * * 1-5"
    min_size = 2
  }
}

# The group's members, once the group exists.
output "web_members" {
  value = nemau_instance_group.web.instance_count
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `max_size` (Number) The autoscaler never goes above this many members, 0 to 50. Changes in place.
- `min_size` (Number) The autoscaler never goes below this many members, 0 to 50. Changes in place.
- `name` (String) A DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 56 characters at most. Changing it replaces the group.
- `network_id` (String) Network of the members. Changing it replaces the group.
- `subnet_id` (String) Subnet of the members. Changing it replaces the group.

### Optional

- `delete_instances_on_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the members when the group is destroyed. Off by default: a group that still has members is then refused at destroy.
- `desired_capacity` (Number) Members the group should run now, between `min_size` and `max_size`. The autoscaler moves it at runtime. When set, Terraform applies the value when the configuration changes it, and does not read the autoscaler's moves back: the state keeps the value last applied. When omitted, the autoscaler owns it and the state shows the platform's value.
- `drain_seconds` (Number) Seconds a member drains before it is removed, 0 to 300. Set by the platform when omitted.
- `health_check` (String) How an unhealthy member is detected: `instance`, the only one for now. Set by the platform when omitted.
- `health_check_grace_seconds` (Number) Seconds a new member is given before its health is checked, 60 to 1800. Set by the platform when omitted.
- `launch_template` (Block, Optional) What each member is created from (required). A change is a new template version. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--launch_template))
- `load_balancer_pool` (Block List) A load balancer pool the members register in. At most 4. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--load_balancer_pool))
- `max_surge` (Number) Extra members a rolling update may start at once, 1 to 10. Set by the platform when omitted.
- `max_unavailable_pct` (Number) Percent of members a rolling update may take down at once, 0 to 50. Set by the platform when omitted.
- `refresh_on_template_change` (Boolean) Start a rolling refresh when the launch template changes, so that the members move to the new version at once, within the group's `max_unavailable_pct` and `max_surge`. Off by default: a template change is then stored, and the members move only when a refresh runs. Changing this flag alone starts nothing.
- `scaling_policy` (Block List) A target-tracking policy: the group adds or removes members to keep the metric near the target. At most 2, one per metric. Only `cpu_percent` is available. Unset values take the platform's defaults. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--scaling_policy))
- `scheduled_action` (Block List) A scheduled action: at each UTC cron time, the group takes the bounds it names. At most 10. Each action sets at least one of the three sizes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--scheduled_action))
- `security_groups` (List of String) Up to 5 security group ids the members are filtered with. Changes in place; removing them all clears the list.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The group's public id.
- `instance_count` (Number) Current number of members.
- `status` (String) State of the group as the platform reports it.
- `template_version` (Number) Version of the launch template the members run.

<a id="nestedblock--launch_template"></a>
### Nested Schema for `launch_template`

Required:

- `image_id` (String) Image id of the members.

Optional:

- `disk_gb` (Number) Disk of the members in GB, 10 to 5000.
- `flavor_id` (String) Flavor id of the members. Exclusive with the custom size: `vcpus`, `ram_mb` and `disk_gb` together.
- `key_name` (String) SSH keypair of the members.
- `ram_mb` (Number) Memory of the members in MB: a multiple of 256, from 1024 to 262144.
- `service_level` (String) `best-effort` (the default) or `99.9%`. After importing a group, the first apply with `service_level` set re-sends the launch template once.
- `user_data` (String, Sensitive) cloud-init document of the members, at most 16 KiB, starting with `#cloud-config`, `#!` or a MIME multipart header. It may hold secrets. The platform never returns it: the provider compares digests. Cannot be removed from a group; replace the group instead.
- `vcpus` (Number) vCPUs of the members, 1 to 64. Set with `ram_mb` and `disk_gb`, instead of `flavor_id`.


<a id="nestedblock--load_balancer_pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `load_balancer_pool`

Required:

- `pool_id` (String) Id of the pool.
- `protocol_port` (Number) Port of the members in the pool, 1 to 65535.


<a id="nestedblock--scaling_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scaling_policy`

Required:

- `metric` (String) `cpu_percent`.
- `target` (Number) Value the metric is kept near, in percent, 10 to 90.

Optional:

- `max_step_in` (Number) Members removed at once, 1 to 5.
- `max_step_out` (Number) Members added at once, 1 to 10.
- `scale_in_cooldown_seconds` (Number) Seconds between two scale-ins, 60 to 3600.
- `scale_in_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the policy may remove members.
- `scale_in_window_seconds` (Number) Seconds of low load before a scale-in, 300 to 3600.
- `scale_out_cooldown_seconds` (Number) Seconds between two scale-outs, 60 to 3600.
- `window_seconds` (Number) Measurement window in seconds, 180 to 900.


<a id="nestedblock--scheduled_action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scheduled_action`

Required:

- `cron` (String) Five cron fields in UTC, for example `0 8 * * 1-5`.

Optional:

- `desired_capacity` (Number) Desired members from this time, 0 to 50.
- `max_size` (Number) Maximum members from this time, 0 to 50.
- `min_size` (Number) Minimum members from this time, 0 to 50.
